context:
TPC variants stress optimizer edge cases: skewed data distributions reveal whether cost-based optimizers handle data skew gracefully; TPC-Havoc tests nested subqueries and complex predicates; Data Vault evaluates enterprise modeling patterns; OBT tests denormalized analytical performance.

Revalidated 2026-10-01. Query counts match the loaded benchmark classes (22 / 220 / 22 / 89; the registry num_queries metadata is stale for TPC-DS-OBT, showing 17). These four suites are rows of the 84-cell live-cloud corpus campaign (28 benchmark rows x 3 warehouses), so progress is read from that campaign's per-cell table and its BigQuery spend ledger rather than from separate runs. Runs inside the campaign's settled limits (6 h per cell, BigQuery cap counted from 2026-09-22) need no new approval; anything outside them needs one that states command, maximum runtime, log path and stop condition. Databricks cells share a 500-table Unity Catalog metastore quota.
description:
Expand live cloud benchmark execution across BigQuery, Databricks, and Snowflake to the TPC variant and experimental benchmark suites:
- TPC-H Skew: 22 queries on data with Zipfian/exponential/normal skew distributions (SF 0.1, 1.0, 10.0)
- TPC-Havoc: 220 query variations stressing engine subquery and predicate evaluation (SF 0.1, 1.0, 10.0)
- TPC-H Data Vault: 22 queries adapted for Hub-Link-Satellite data modeling (SF 0.1, 1.0, 10.0)
- TPC-DS-OBT: 89 queries adapted for One Big Table / de-normalized denormalization (SF 1.0)

Execute across BigQuery, Databricks, and Snowflake at the supported scale factors.
Verify 100% query pass rate and valid bundle structure.
